basis: Loss of cortical recognition of objects by touch is a neurologic perceptual deficit.
Cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy define disease; muscle wasting and weakness reflect denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Alphavirus infection with inflammatory polyarthritis in well over 30%; joint inflammation may persist for months. Transient rash excluded.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss.
Congenital absence of a limb or limb segment is a structural defect of the locomotor system.
Disease of atrial cardiac electrical conduction; associated cardiomyopathy remains within the cardiovascular axis.
Primary skeletal muscle dystrophy; hearing impairment occurs in 6/33 patients, below 30%. Facial weakness does not establish peripheral nerve disease.
Pathologic enlargement of subcutaneous adipose tissue; secondary lymphedema is a complication, not an independent defining axis.
Disordered calcium deposition occludes small vessels and causes skin necrosis. CKD and hyperparathyroidism are underlying conditions; secondary infections are separate.
Brain malformations and developmental impairment define syndrome; strabismus occurs in 80-99%, refractive impairment and joint hypermobility in 30-79%.
Skeletal dysplasia, valvular disease and abnormal dentition define syndrome; ptosis occurs in 80-99% and supports ocular involvement.
Chronic gonococcal infection of the cervix; the reproductive site has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Site-unspecified malignant neoplasm; anaplasia describes differentiation. No shared organ axis can be assigned across its diverse subtypes.
Neoplasm arising in the jejunal wall; lymphoma is only one possible histology and does not define the umbrella.
Innate antiviral immunodeficiency; organ-specific viral infections are separate diseases. Encephalopathy is occasional; isolated ALT elevation does not establish liver damage.
Selective antibody deficiency; many patients are asymptomatic. Respiratory and gastrointestinal infections and autoimmune disorders are separate associated diseases.
Low-grade astrocytic neoplasm arising in the central nervous system.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes bronchiectasis and sinus disease; intrinsic middle-ear clearance failure with chronic otitis/hearing dysfunction is common (>30%) in PCD.
KRT5-related reticulate skin pigmentation disorder; no evidence of systemic metabolic disease or other organ dysfunction.
Inherited B12 absorption defect causes megaloblastic anemia; dementia and learning disability occur in 30-79%. Intrinsic factor absence does not imply gastric mucosal damage.
Tricarboxylic acid cycle disorder defined by neurodegeneration and retinal dystrophy; hearing impairment occurs in 2/8 patients, below 30%.
Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection of the anterior nasal airway; systemic toxin complications are not common in this localized form.
Inherited thyrotropin resistance causing congenital hypothyroidism; no common extra-endocrine damage is established for this subtype.
Definition specifies craniofacial skeletal hypoplasia, lower-eyelid coloboma and microtia; these are intrinsic developmental abnormalities.
Primary mixed epithelial and mesenchymal neoplasm of the uterine corpus; reproductive organs have no axis.
